findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the shared-ledger-over-layer-reorder decision (and the 'completion policy must keep seeing calls' constraint) in an ADR or AGENTS.md note near src/rebar/llm/, not only in the ticket.

Scope lists only source and test files; no doc/ADR artifact.
findings.finding: The plan makes a novel architectural decision — a SHARED ToolCallLedger between the guard and memo layers instead of reordering layers — but names no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc capture for why shared-ledger was chosen over layer reordering, despite this being the load-bearing rationale.
scenarios: A future maintainer sees Guard->Memo->Steering order pinned and a ledger threaded through both layers, and re-litigates the layer-reorder option that this plan deliberately rejected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reason through (and add a test for) served_streak under a CONCURRENT parallel tool-call batch: confirm the increment-before-await / reset-after-inner-run ordering cannot spuriously trip arm 2 or drop a reset, and pin the intended semantics (e.g. dedup the streak per run_step like the ratio arm, or snapshot the streak once per step).
evidence: Approach: arm 2 is 'a served-streak backstop ... checked at call entry, before increment'
runaway_guard.py: guard does `ledger.served_streak += 1` then `await self.wrapped.call_tool(...)`; ToolCallLedger.record_executed sets `served_streak = 0` inside the inner memo layer
Memo docstring (agent_call.py _memo_toolsets): 'pydantic-ai runs a turn's tool calls concurrently' — the reason the memo needs per-signature asyncio.Locks

Testing addresses concurrency only for the ratio arm ('a parallel batch shares one step number, so only its first-observed call pays the O(window) ratio'); no parallel-batch case for the served_streak backstop
findings.finding: The served-streak backstop (arm 2) mutates a single shared int (ledger.served_streak) across CONCURRENT tool-call coroutines without the per-step dedup that protects arm 1, and the plan neither reasons through nor tests this concurrent case. The guard increments served_streak at call entry (before the inner await) while record_executed resets it only after the wrapped tool runs; a parallel batch (which the memo layer's own docstring says pydantic-ai issues) can interleave increments-before-resets, so the streak can momentarily over-count and either trip arm 2 spuriously or under-count and miss a bound within one turn.
scenarios: A verifier turn issues a parallel batch of cache-served re-reads interleaved with one memo-miss execution; the increment-then-await ordering lets the served_streak see a stale/over-counted value across coroutines
A single turn with >= REPETITION_WINDOW concurrent cached calls where the intended reset from an interleaved executed call is observed too late
